get.summary: Whether the server still needs its first administrator, and whether its environment gives the setup code.

post.summary: Creates the first administrator (or, with Sfe:Setup:Recover, restores one) and signs it in.
post.description:
Needs the setup code of the server's environment (`Sfe:Setup:Code`, at least 12 characters): without it
the server cannot be set up from the web. Refused once an administrator exists, unless
`Sfe:Setup:Recover` is on. A new install (no account yet) set up from the server's own computer, in the
browser SFE opened or with the link its console shows (its token in the header `X-SFE-Setup-Link`),
needs no code (`codeRequired` false in `GetSetup`, unless `Sfe:Setup:LocalWithoutCode` is off).
`fastSignIn` turns on `Sfe:FastSignIn` for the browser SFE opens when it starts.

post.summary: Checks the setup code and answers the installation settings with a token for the other installation routes.
post.description:
The token goes in the `X-SFE-Installation` header; it lasts an hour, and ends when the setup code
changes. A new install set up from the server's own computer needs no code (see `CompleteSetup`). Once
the server has an administrator, every installation route also needs a signed-in server administrator
(401 without a session, 403 for other accounts).

get.summary: The library folder, listening address and ffmpeg of the server, and which of them its environment decides.
get.description: Needs the token of `CheckInstallationCode` in the `X-SFE-Installation` header.

put.summary: Saves the library folder, listening address, ffmpeg or the server's mode into the installation file (data/installation.json).
put.description:
Needs the token of `CheckInstallationCode` in the `X-SFE-Installation` header. A new folder or ffmpeg
starts the libraries again at once; a new address applies after a restart (`restartRequired`). Values
set by the server's environment variables or command line cannot be changed here. The mode (`Sfe:Mode`)
goes from Local to External here, never back once the server has its administrator; Local is only chosen
from a browser on the server's own computer.

get.summary: The folders of the server's disks, to pick the library folder or ffmpeg's folder.
get.description: Needs the token of `CheckInstallationCode` in the `X-SFE-Installation` header. Without `path`: the drives and usual places.

get.summary: Whether the install waits for its update to this version, with the changes since its version.
get.description:
While an update is due (`required`, `running`, `failed`), or the install belongs to a later version
(`newer`), every other route answers 503 `migration-required`. `log` and the text of `error` name
folders and servers: they are given only with the setup code in the header `X-SFE-Setup-Code` (as the
update page sends it once typed); without it `log` is empty and `error` only says that there is one.

post.summary: Starts updating the databases and settings to this version; needs the setup code (Sfe:Setup:Code).
post.description: Runs in the background: poll `GET api/migration` until its status is `none` (done) or `failed`.

post.summary: Makes a backup (zip) of the databases and configuration files before the update; needs the setup code.
post.description: Answers the link the browser downloads it from, once. Only while an update is due: afterwards, Administration › System.

get.summary: Downloads a backup made by CreateMigrationBackup (once).
Who is signed in, in which space, and what the sign-in page offers.

post.summary: Signs in with a name and password.
post.description:
`remember` keeps the session after the browser closes (for `Sfe:Security:SessionDays` without use). A
Local server (`Sfe:Mode`) lets only administrators in (server administrators, members of a space's
Administrators group): others get 400 `local-administrators-only`.

post.summary: Signs out.
Picks the space a visitor without an account browses, among those open to guests (signs out first).
Switches the signed-in account to another of its spaces.

get.summary: Signs the server's only administrator in with the one-time link of the browser SFE opened at start, then opens the app.
get.description:
Only with `Sfe:FastSignIn` (Administration › System › Start-up), from the server's own computer, while
the server has a single enabled administrator. The link (`token`) is made when SFE starts, works once
and for 1 minute. Whatever happens, the answer sends the browser to
the app.

post.summary: Asks for a one-time code to recover a server administrator's account; the server shows it only where it runs.
post.description:
For a server administrator locked out (wrong passwords from someone else) or who forgot the password.
The code appears in the server's console and in `recovery-code.txt` beside the setup code file, for
15 minutes; asking again shows the same code. The answer is the
same whatever the name, so it doesn't tell which accounts exist.

post.summary: Sets a new password with the recovery code, unlocks the account and signs it in.
post.description: The account's other sessions end. The code works once.

put.summary: Changes the password of the signed-in local account; its other sessions end.

get.summary: Every right, with those the server and the space switch off.
get.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

get.summary: Accounts: every one for server administrators (`all=true`), else those of the space.
get.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

post.summary: Creates a local account.
post.description: A space's administrator can only put it in that space's groups, and cannot make server administrators.

put.summary: Changes an account (a new password or status ends its sessions).
put.description:
Server administrators replace every group of the account (`groupIds`: those of all its spaces). A
space's administrator changes only the account's groups in that space, unless the account belongs to
that space alone and is no server administrator.

delete.summary: Deletes an account, or (for a space's administrator) takes it out of the space.

get.summary: The groups of the space, with their rights and members; those of every space with `all=true` (server administrators).
get.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

post.summary: Creates a group in the space.
post.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

put.summary: Changes a group's name, directory group, rights and members.
put.description:
The Guests group cannot get a right guests may never have. Only server administrators add accounts that
are in none of the space's groups yet. `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

delete.summary: Deletes a group (not a built-in one).
delete.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

get.summary: Guest access of the space and the rights switched off in it.

put.summary: Opens the space to visitors without an account (with its Guests group's rights), or closes it.

get.summary: The signed-in account's access tokens, revoked and expired ones too, newest first.

post.summary: Makes an access token for programs calling the API as the signed-in account.
post.description:
The answer holds the whole token (`secret`) once: it is never shown again, only its first characters
(`prefix`). `expires` (UTC) defaults to the longest life the server allows; `tenantId` limits the token to
one space the account reaches; `rights` limits it to some of the account's rights (none: all of them, as
they are at each use). 403 when tokens are turned off, 409 when the account holds as many as allowed.

delete.summary: Revokes one of the signed-in account's access tokens: it stops working at once.

post.summary: Revokes every access token of the signed-in account; answers how many were in use.

get.summary: The access tokens of the accounts one administers, revoked and expired ones too, newest first.
get.description:
Server administrators see every account's tokens; a space's administrators those of the accounts of the
spaces where they hold `access.tokens`, but no server administrator's.

delete.summary: Revokes the access token of an account one administers.

get.summary: The space's folder rules: what a group, or one account, may do in a folder and below it.
get.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

put.summary: Sets the level of a group or an account at a folder (`hidden`, `read`, `write`), or removes its rule (`level: null`); answers every rule.
put.description:
The nearest rule above a path decides each group's and account's level there; a group without one has
`write`. An account rule only adds to what its groups give. A space has at most
250 rules. `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

post.summary: Moves the rules of a folder that is no longer there (and of its sub-folders) to another folder.
post.description:
For a folder moved or renamed outside SFE. 409 while `from` still exists, or when `to` (or a folder
below it) has rules already. `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

get.summary: Who may see and change a folder: every group and account of the space, and visitors.
get.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

get.summary: The sub-folders of a folder of the space, for choosing where a rule goes (every folder, whatever rules apply to the asker).
get.description: `tenant`: the id of another space than the request's one (server administrators only).

get.summary: Every space (tenant), with its library folder and its numbers of accounts and groups.

post.summary: Creates a space on a folder inside the allowed roots, with its own index, tags, settings and groups.
post.description:
The index of its library goes to `Sfe:Tenants:ConnectionString` (with `{tenant}` for its short name),
else next to the first space's (SQLite: `tenants/{slug}.db` beside its file; SQL Server: database
`{database}_{slug}` on the same server, which the server's account must be allowed to create). Its
caches go under `{CacheDirectory}/tenants/{slug}`.

get.summary: Folders a space's library folder can be chosen in (`Sfe:Tenants:AllowedRoots`, else the configured root).
get.description: Without `path`, the allowed roots; with one, its sub-folders (hidden ones left out).

put.summary: Renames a space, opens or closes it to guests, disables it, and sets the rights nobody gets there.

delete.summary: Deletes a space's groups and settings; its index database and caches stay on the disk.

get.summary: Settings the web client needs, with the session's own preferences and rights.
Lists a folder of the library (folders first).
The folders before and after a folder in its parent.
get.description:
Pass the `sort` and `desc` the parent is listed with (as for `/browse`): the siblings follow that order.
The library root has no siblings.

post.summary: The first pictures of folders, shown on their cards.
post.description:
Takes up to 100 folders and returns, for each one that exists, its first
`Browse:FolderPictures` images and videos in name order (videos only when thumbnails are available).
Only a folder's own files count; a folder without any, or a setting of 0, gets an empty list.

get.summary: Searches the file index.
get.description:
`,` separates alternatives (OR), a space separates required terms (AND), `-term` excludes,
`s:<10mb` / `s:>=1gb` / `s:700mb` filter by size, `e:mp4` by extension, `w:>=1920` / `h:<720` /
`r:1920x1080` by resolution, `d:>10m` by duration, `type:image` / `type:video` / `type:audio` /
`type:other` by kind of file, a leading `*` matches the whole path instead of the file name, `t:name`
(or `tag:"two words"`) finds files with a tag or any tag inheriting from it, and `special:untagged`
files without tags. A `-` before any term (`-e:mp4`, `-s:>1gb`, `-w:1920`, `-t:name`) finds the files
that term doesn't. Files with a hidden tag (Archived) are left out unless the search names that tag.

`sort` is `path` (default, grouped by folder), `name`, `modified`, `size`, `type`, `duration` or
`resolution` (width × height); `desc` reverses it. The last two list the files whose value is known
first, then the others by path, in both directions.
Pages follow each other by passing the previous page's `next` as `after`, with the same sort.
The first page also gives `total`, the number of matches counted up to 10,000 (`totalCapped` when there
are more); the next pages leave it null.

get.summary: Streams a file (supports HTTP range requests for media seeking).
get.description: `download=true` asks the browser to save it, which needs the right `files.download`.

get.summary: Whether a picture is animated (GIF, APNG, WebP or AVIF with more than one frame).
get.description:
Read from the file's structure, without decoding it. The listings ask before playing the original of an
image they show through its thumbnail, on hover.

post.summary: A link to a file that works without signing in, for a while: for external players.
post.description:
The link (`api/files/shared/{token}/{name}`, relative to the app) works for
`Player:LinkLifetimeMinutes`. It stops working earlier when the account that asked for it changes its
password, is disabled, or loses the right to view files or use external players.

get.summary: Streams the file of a link made by `CreateFileLink` (the token stands for the sign-in; range requests supported).
JPEG preview of a video or image.
Groups of indexed files with the same size and fingerprint, biggest first.
get.description: Only files of `path` and below are compared. Pass the `next` value of a page as `after` to get the next one; the first page also carries totals.

post.summary: Deletes a copy from the disk after adding its tags to an identical copy that is kept.
post.description: The two files are compared byte for byte first, and paths leading to the same file (folder links) are refused. 409 when turned off (`FileTracking:Duplicates:AllowRemove`) or when the file cannot be deleted.

get.summary: Groups of videos with the same pictures but other bytes (other resolution, bitrate, codec, trimmed), from the last comparison.
get.description: Only groups with a video in `path` or below are listed. Each video's `match` is its share of matching frames with the first video of the group. Pass the `next` value of a page as `after` to get the next one; the first page also carries totals. Carries the comparison's status: start one with `POST /api/similar-videos`.

post.summary: Compares the fingerprints of the indexed videos in the background (made with their trickplay); does nothing while a comparison runs.
Saves an edited picture as a new file of the library; the original is never changed.
post.description:
The body is the edited picture itself, as the web client's editor encoded it: JPEG, PNG or WebP (at most
200 MB; the format is read from its bytes, not from `Content-Type`).
`path` is the original. The new file goes to `Editor:OutputFolder` under the original's own folders
(`Photos/2024/beach.jpg` → `Edited/Photos/2024/beach.jpg`), or next to the original as
`beach (edited).jpg` when the setting is empty or the original is already in that folder. An existing
name gets ` (2)`, ` (3)`... The file is indexed at once. Answers 201 with its path and size in pixels.

put.summary: Saves an edited picture over the original.
put.description:
The body is the edited picture, in the original's own format (JPEG, PNG or WebP; 400 otherwise: save a
copy instead). Needs `If-Match` with the version the editor started from (`*`: whatever is there now):
428 (`version-required`) without it, 412 (`file-changed`) when the
picture changed meanwhile. The previous version goes to the trash at the first save of an editing
`session` (not in a space that always deletes for good); the picture keeps its tags. 409 for a link
(`file-is-link`), a read-only file (`read-only`) or a scan running
(`scan-running`). Answers the picture's size in pixels, its new version (also the
ETag) and time.

get.summary: The picture's version, and whether the caller may save the edited picture over it.

post.summary: Moves or copies files and folders between the library and a connection, in the background.
post.description:
`kind` `move` or `copy`; `from`: a `connection` (null: the library) and its `paths` (at most
1000); `to`: a `connection` (null: the library) and the folder `path`. Within the library
use `api/files/jobs`, within one connection `api/connections/{id}/files/transfer`: 400 here. A connection
the caller may not use answers 404, one it only reads 403 when written to (the target, a move's source), 409
when it cannot be opened (sign in again). Answers 202 with the job, followed through `api/files/jobs/{id}`;
`fromConnection` and `toConnection` name its sides. Files are verified (size, and the content hash when a side
gives one) before a move takes its source away: into SFE's trash in the library, the provider's in a
connection.

post.summary: Starts again the failed items of one of the caller's ended transfers.
post.description:
Starts again, as a new job, the items of an ended transfer that failed or were not reached, with the same
places and conflict choice, for 24 hours after it ended (and while the server runs): a folder already at the
target is gone into, a file there of the same size (and, for a move, content hash) counts as transferred, a
file whose writing broke is written again from its start. Access is checked again as
`api/files/jobs/transfer` checks it. Answers 202 with the new job (its own id, followed through
`api/files/jobs/{id}`); 404 for a job that is not one of the
caller's transfers; 409 `job-running` while it runs, `nothing-to-retry` when nothing failed (or it was
started again already, or is too old).

get.summary: A file inside an EPUB book (a chapter, a style, a picture, a font), for the reader.
get.description:
`book` is the book's path, UTF-8 in base64url, so that the links inside the book (`../images/cover.jpg`)
resolve under it. `entry` is the file's name in the book's zip (any case when it isn't found as
written); 404 for one that isn't there, a folder, or one larger than
64 MB. Read from the zip as asked, never unpacked; sandboxed as
the library's files are.

post.summary: Extracts an archive (zip, 7z, rar, tar, gz…), all of it or the entries chosen, in the background.
post.description:
Starts an extraction job and answers its first state (202), followed as moves and copies are
(`GET api/files/jobs/:id`, `answer`, `cancel`). `newFolder` (default): into a new folder named after the
archive (after its one top folder when it has one), never mixed with what is there; else straight into
`target`, where name clashes are asked as `conflicts` says. `folders` and `files` (at most
10000, ids of the archive's listing: its list must have been read, else 409
`archive-reading`) choose what is extracted, each from its own name. Names leading out of the folder,
links, names the system refuses, and files claiming more than `Files:Archives:MaxCompressionRatio` times
their packed size are left out and listed in the result. A protected archive needs `unlock` (or
`password`): a wrong one fails the job before anything stays. Cancelled or failed, nothing half written
stays. At most 10 a minute per caller.

post.summary: A link that plays a Flash movie (`.swf`) in the viewer, opening the files of its folder to it, read only.
post.description:
The link (`api/files/flash/{token}/{name}`, relative to the app) works for
12 hours, and stops earlier when the account changes its password, is
disabled, or loses the right to view the files. 404 when the library doesn't play Flash movies
(`Player:Flash`) or the file isn't a `.swf`.

get.summary: A file of a Flash movie's folder (the movie, its levels, music, data), for Ruffle: the token stands for the sign-in.
get.description:
`entry` is relative to the movie's folder; its subfolders are open, nothing above it. Answered to any
origin (the player's frame has none) without credentials, sandboxed as the library's files are.

get.summary: Server-sent events: `changed` with `{ path, origin }` (and `connection` for a connection's) each time a folder is changed through SFE; `keepAlive` with `{ state }`; `trash`; `ping`.
get.description:
Open with `EventSource`; `origin` is the `X-SFE-Tab` header of the request that changed it (a tab
skips its own). `keepAlive` comes first, then each time keep alive's state changes: `none` (off, or
nothing pinged), `ok`, `failing`; no folder nor error is named. `trash` (to callers with files.delete or
files.deletePermanently) when something came into or left the trash: ask its count again. A `ping` event
after 25 s without anything keeps it open; it ends after
10 minutes and the browser opens it again. 12 at once per
caller (429).

get.summary: Searches the library's index of a connection's files.
get.description:
The search of `GET api/search` (same terms, sorts, `after` paging and `total` on the first page), on the
library's index of the connection: paths are relative to the connection's root, `path` is the folder searched
with everything below it. The index holds what the provider tells when listing: width, height and duration
are mostly unknown, so `w:`, `h:`, `r:` and `d:` rarely match. `coverage` says how much of the connection the
index holds: `none` (not indexed in this library yet: nothing found, the first sync starts), `partial` (being
listed, or not synced for a while) or `complete`. Folder rules apply: hidden folders and files are in no page
nor count. Names sort as the connection's listings sort them; files indexed before that key existed come
after the others, by path.

get.summary: Progress of the current or last index scan.

post.summary: Starts indexing a folder recursively in the background.
post.description:
Folders excluded from scans (`Scan:ExcludedFolders`) are skipped and what the index has of them stays
as it is; a folder excluded itself, or inside an excluded one, is refused (400).

delete.summary: Cancels the running scan.

get.summary: What the index holds of a folder and its sub-folders: counts of folders, files and tagged files.

delete.summary: Removes a folder and its sub-folders from the index; the files stay on the disk.
delete.description:
Tagged files are kept as missing files with their tags (unless relinking is off): scanning the folder
again gives the tags back. With `exclude=true` the folder is also added to `Scan:ExcludedFolders`, so
that scans of its parents skip it (not for the library root). 409 while a scan runs.

get.summary: The folders kept out of scans, trickplay or thumbnails in the space, with which of them.

put.summary: Keeps a folder (with its sub-folders) out of scans, trickplay or thumbnails, or lets them in again.
put.description:
Changes the space's `Scan:ExcludedFolders`, `Trickplay:ExcludedFolders` and
`Thumbnails:ExcludedFolders`. A folder no longer on the disk can only be taken off them. What is already
indexed or made stays: scans keep the folder's index rows as they are. A folder excluded through a
listed parent can only be let in again by taking the parent off the list (400). Answers what the folder
is kept out of afterwards.

get.summary: Lists tags, or finds the ones whose name, shorthand or alias contains `q`.
get.description: Names starting with `q` come first. `descendants` lists the tags inheriting from a match.

post.summary: Creates a tag.

get.summary: Most used tags, last searched tags, tags of the last viewed files, and random other tags.

delete.summary: Forgets the searched and viewed tags (the sidebar's history lists).

get.summary: A tag with its aliases and parent tags.

put.summary: Replaces a tag's name, shorthand, aliases, parents, color and properties.

delete.summary: Deletes a tag and removes it from every file. Built-in tags cannot be deleted.

get.summary: Tags of a file, also grouped by category tag.

post.summary: Adds and removes tags on one or more files.
post.description: Files that are not indexed yet are indexed (their folder only) before being tagged.

get.summary: Tags of the files of a folder (or a folder tree), or of the matches of a search, with the number of files having each.
get.description: Without `q`: the indexed files of the folder `path`, and of its sub-folders with `recursive`. With `q`: what that search finds in `path`.

post.summary: Adds and removes tags on every file of a folder (or a folder tree), or on every match of a search.
post.description: A folder is indexed first (with its sub-folders when `recursive`), so that its files not indexed yet are tagged too; that is refused (409) while a scan runs. A search changes the files it finds. The files are changed by batches: a request that is cancelled keeps the batches already written.

post.summary: Records that a file was viewed: its tags become the last viewed tags.

get.summary: The default tags of a folder: its own, and those it gets from its parents.
get.description: Every file entering the folder or one of its sub-folders (scanned, created, uploaded, copied or moved there) gets them once.

put.summary: Adds and removes default tags of a folder, and optionally on the files already in it and its sub-folders.
put.description: With `addToFiles` / `removeFromFiles`, the files already in the folder tree get the added tags or lose the removed ones, as `POST api/file-tags/scope` with `recursive` does, before the folder's default tags change (refused with 409 while a scan runs: nothing changes).

get.summary: State of the background trickplay generation.

post.summary: Looks for videos without trickplay in the configured folders now.

get.summary: Videos being processed, the first waiting ones (`limit`, default 100) and the last ones finished.

post.summary: Which of the given videos are waiting for their trickplay or being processed.
post.description:
Takes up to 5000 library paths; videos with nothing to do are left out of
`files`. `running` tells whether the job is busy at all: the client may check less often when not.

get.summary: Trickplay of a video: its description, or one of its sheets with `?sheet=n`.
get.description:
404 when the video has no trickplay yet. A video of the configured folders is then queued, ahead of the
background pass, unless `queue=false` (a thumbnail preview only shows what exists). Sheets are JPEG
images; their URL should carry the description's `version` (e.g. `&v=`): they are cached by the browser.

get.summary: Whether a video can be played converted by the server, and its length.
get.description: 404 when streaming is off (`Streaming:Mode`), ffmpeg is missing, or `path` is not a video of the library.

get.summary: A video converted by ffmpeg while it plays (H.264 and AAC in fragmented MP4), from `t` seconds.
get.description:
For browsers that can't play the file itself. The response has no length and no ranges: to seek, ask
again with another `t` (its times start at 0 there). `id` names the player: a new request with the same
`id` stops its earlier stream. 503 while the server converts `Streaming:MaxStreams` videos already.

get.summary: The videos the server converts now, in every library, with who watches them.
The background tasks with their state and last run, the schedules with their next run.
get.description:
Tasks: `scan`, `trickplay`, `similarVideos`, `thumbnails`. `automaticNextRun` is when a task runs by
itself next (trickplay's periodic check), whatever the schedules. Weekly schedules follow the clock of
the server's `timeZone`.

post.summary: Starts a task now (thumbnails can't be started: listings ask for them).
post.description: A scan covers `path` (relative to the library root; empty: the whole library). 409 when it already runs, or is turned off; a trickplay pass asked for while one runs follows it (202).

post.summary: Stops a running task.
post.description:
A scan keeps what it indexed so far. Trickplay stops its pass and the player's queue (the periodic
passes go on). Thumbnails drops the renders running and waiting. 409 when it wasn't running.

post.summary: Schedules a task: once, every N minutes from a start, or on days of the week at a time.

put.summary: Changes a schedule; its next run is worked out again from now.

delete.summary: Deletes a schedule; its past runs stay in the history.

post.summary: The next runs of a schedule being edited, or its validation errors.

get.summary: Runs of the background tasks, newest first, without their logs.
get.description: Optionally of one `task`. Pages of `limit` runs (default 50, at most 500); pass `next` as `before` for the following page.

delete.summary: Deletes the history of finished runs.

get.summary: A run with its log (live while it runs).
Tagged files a scan no longer found, with the indexed files that may be them.
get.description: Scans relink them on their own when exactly one likely new place is indexed; the others wait here until relinked by hand, forgotten, or kept longer than the retention.

delete.summary: Forgets every missing file and their tags.

post.summary: Relinks now the missing files that have exactly one likely new place (done after every scan).
Gives the tags of a missing file to a file of the library, and forgets the missing file.

delete.summary: Forgets a missing file and its tags.

post.summary: Creates an empty file.
post.description:
Creates the empty file `name` in the folder `path` (never over anything: 409 `file-exists` when the
name is taken, even by an item the caller doesn't see) and indexes it. Answers the new file as listings
show it; 400 for a name that can't be used, 404 when the folder is not there, 409 `scan-running`
during a scan.

post.summary: Creates a folder.
post.description:
Creates the folder `name` in the folder `path`, and indexes it at once when its parent is indexed.
Answers the new folder as listings show it; 400 for a name that can't be used (with the reason), 404
when the folder `path` is not there, 409 `file-exists` when something of that name is (even one the
caller doesn't see), 409 `scan-running` while a scan runs over the folder.

post.summary: Renames a file or folder, in its folder.
post.description:
Renames `path` to `name` in the same folder. A case-only change (`photo.jpg` → `Photo.jpg`) is allowed
on Windows. What SFE keeps by path follows: the index (tags), folder access rules, quick links, settings
naming folders, schedules, thumbnails and trickplay. A folder can be renamed only by someone who may
rename everywhere below it. Answers the renamed item; 400 for a name that can't be used, 404, 403, 409
`file-exists`, `scan-running` or `folder-rules` (rules are set where the folder would go),
500 when the disk refuses (a file in use, no write access).

post.summary: Deletes files and folders, to the trash or for good.
post.description:
Deletes each of `paths` (at most 1000): to the space's trash, or for good with `permanent`
(always when `Files:DeletePermanently` is on, which then needs `files.deletePermanently`). A link is
deleted as a link. Answers 200 with a result per path: `done` (with `trashId` when it went to the
trash), `notFound` (also what the caller doesn't see), `forbidden`, `scanRunning`, `trashUnavailable` (a
folder with links on another drive than the trash: delete it permanently instead), `failed` (in use, no
write access), with a message.

post.summary: Who would gain access to folders if they moved there.
post.description: Each group, and each account with rules, that would see or change more of a moved folder than now: the client asks for a confirmation (and offers to keep the current access) before starting the move.

post.summary: Moves or copies files and folders, in the background.
post.description:
Starts a job and answers its first state (202). `conflicts` says what to do when the target holds an
item of the same name: `ask` (the job waits: `GET` shows the `conflict`, `POST /answer` replies),
`replace` (needs the right to delete there: the replaced item goes to the trash), `skip`, `keepBoth`
(` (2)` added). Moves keep tags, folder rules (`keepAccess` pins each group's current access), quick
links and caches; copies never follow links, leave out folders the caller may not see, and get the tags
of their originals with `keepTags`. Results per item in `results`.

get.summary: The caller's moves, copies and extractions, running and recent.

post.summary: Compresses files and folders into one zip in a folder of the library, in the background.
post.description:
Starts a compression job and answers its first state (202), followed as moves and copies are. `paths` (1
to 10,000), `target` the folder the zip goes into, `name` (`.zip` added; default: the
only item's name, else their folder's), `level` 0 (stored) to 9 (default 6), `skipCompressed` (default
true: pictures, videos, archives… stored whatever the level), `password` (AES-256; the names stay
readable). What the caller may not see is left out silently, links and folders they may not download are
named in `SFE - left out.txt`. One compression at a time on the server
(`Files:Archives:CompressJobs`). A name taken in the target is asked as `conflicts` says. Its result
tells the ratio achieved.

get.summary: One of the caller's moves or copies.

post.summary: Answers a job's question about a name clash (`forAll`: the same for the next ones).
Stops a move or copy: what is done stays, nothing half copied does.

get.summary: The space's trash, newest first.
get.description: Pages of at most 200; `before` is the `next` of the previous page.

delete.summary: Deletes for good everything of the trash the caller may.

get.summary: How many files and folders of the trash the caller sees, for the sidebar's Trash link.
get.description: Counted up to 99; `more` when there are more.

post.summary: Puts a file or folder of the trash back where it was.
post.description:
Back with the tags of its files and a folder's access rules; its folder is made again if it is gone, and
` (2)` is added to the name when it is taken there. Answers the restored item; 404, 409
`scan-running`, 500 when the disk refuses.

delete.summary: Deletes a file or folder of the trash for good.

post.summary: Which of these names are already taken in the folder.
post.description: Asked before uploading, so that the person decides about names taken (Replace, Skip, Keep both) before sending anything. At most 1000 names.

post.summary: Starts an upload.
post.description:
Checks the folder, the name (a path below the folder for a folder upload: its folders are made at the
finish), the size (`Files:Uploads:MaxFileSizeMegabytes`, the free space kept) and answers the upload
(201) with its `id`. Then `PUT /<id>?offset=` sends the bytes in chunks of at most
16 MB, and `POST /<id>/finish` puts the file in the folder.

get.summary: The caller's unfinished uploads; with `all` (right `settings.files`), everyone's.
One of the caller's unfinished uploads: how much the server has.

put.summary: Appends a chunk (the body) at `offset`.
put.description:
`offset` must be the bytes the server has: another one answers 409 with the upload, to resend from
there (a reply lost on the way). A chunk passing the size, or 16 MB,
is refused (400). Answers the upload.

delete.summary: Cancels an unfinished upload (the caller's, or anyone's with `settings.files`): what it received is removed.

post.summary: Puts a fully sent upload into its folder.
post.description:
`conflicts` says what to do when the name is taken: `ask` (409 `file-exists`, to ask and
finish again), `replace` (the file there goes to the trash; needs the right to delete there), `skip`
(the upload is removed, 204), `keepBoth` (` (2)` added). Answers the new file as listings show it.

post.summary: Names the files and folders of a zip; answers the link that downloads it.
post.description:
At most 10,000 items. Each must be seen, openable and downloadable; a folder brings
everything in it. The link works once, for the caller, within 2
minutes. 429 when the caller already downloads 2 zips; 400 when the space's
`Files:MaxArchiveMegabytes` is smaller than what the index knows of them.

get.summary: Downloads a zip named by CreateArchive (once).
get.description:
Written while it is sent (no size known in advance). Links are not followed; folders the caller doesn't
see are left out; links, unreadable files and folders the caller may not download are listed in
“SFE - left out.txt” inside the zip. A zip passing `Files:MaxArchiveMegabytes` (the index was
behind) is cut off: the download fails.

get.summary: A file's or folder's properties: dates, size, attributes, and what the index knows of it.
How many files and folders, and how many bytes, the index has below a folder.

post.summary: Counts a folder's files, folders and bytes on the disk, in the background.
post.description:
Answers the job, followed with `GET jobs/<id>`. Links are not followed; at most
2,000,000 entries (`capped`). One count per caller at a time: a new one stops
the previous.

post.summary: Reads a file whole for its checksum (`sha256`, `sha1` or `md5`), in the background.
post.description: Answers the job, followed with `GET jobs/<id>`. One checksum per caller at a time: a new one stops the previous.

get.summary: One of the caller's counts or checksums: its progress, then its result.

delete.summary: Stops one of the caller's counts or checksums.

get.summary: A file's content as text, with its encoding, line ending, version and what the caller may do with it.
get.description:
At most 10 MB: larger files answer 413 (`too-large`), files that aren't
text 415 (`not-text`). A byte order mark gives the encoding; otherwise valid UTF-8 is UTF-8 and
anything else windows-1252; `encoding` (`utf-8`, `windows-1252`, `utf-16le`, `utf-16be`) reads it
otherwise (Reopen with encoding). `access` says whether the caller may save over it, save a copy or
download it.

put.summary: Saves text over a file, as an OS text editor does.
put.description:
Needs `If-Match` with the version the editor started from (`*`: whatever is there now): 428
(`version-required`) without it, 412 (`file-changed`) when the file changed meanwhile. The text is
written in `encoding` with `lineEnding` (`lf`, `crlf`, `cr`); characters the encoding can't hold answer
422 (`not-encodable`, with `characters`). The previous version goes to the trash at the first save
of an editing `session` (not in a space that always deletes for good); the file keeps its tags. 409 for
a link (`file-is-link`), a read-only file (`read-only`) or a scan running
(`scan-running`). Answers the new version (also the ETag).

post.summary: Saves text as a new file.
post.description:
Creates the file `name` in the folder `path` with the text in `encoding` and `lineEnding`, never over
anything (409 `file-exists`, even for an item the caller doesn't see). Answers the new
file as listings show it; 400 for a name that can't be used, 422 (`not-encodable`) as when saving.

get.summary: A part of a text file of any size, at whole lines: large files and logs.
get.description:
About `length` bytes (default 256 KB, at most 1024 KB) from `offset`, or
the last ones without an offset (`offset=-1`): cut after the first and the last line break, so that
`end` is where the next part starts. Decoded as the whole file would be, or in `encoding`. 415
(`not-text`) for a binary file.

get.summary: The version of a text file now: has it changed since it was opened?
get.description:
Read only when its size or time differ from those of `known` (the version the viewer has). Files over
10 MB have no version (null): only their size and time.

get.summary: The video a subtitle file belongs to: next to it, named as it is without its language marks.
get.description:
`Film.en.forced.srt` belongs to `Film.en.forced`, `Film.en` or `Film` with one of the library's video
extensions, in that order. `path` is null when there is none, or none the caller may see. A few file
checks, not a listing of the folder.

get.summary: A folder of an archive (zip, 7z, rar, tar), in pages: its folders first, then its files, by name.
get.description:
`folder` is a folder's id (from a previous answer; the root without it) or `at` its path inside the
archive. The first question about an archive reads its list once, in the background: 202 with the
entries read so far until it is ready (ask again). `after` is the previous page's `next`; `limit` at
most 1000 (default 200). An archive not read yet starts its read,
30 a minute per caller at most (429 past it). 409 (`not-explorable`)
for a file that isn't an archive SFE explores (one file compressed alone, a compressed tar over
`Files:Archives:MaxCompressedTarMegabytes`, a name its bytes deny); 422 (`archive-unreadable`) when it
can't be read now. `complete` false: the list stopped (`stopped` says why).

get.summary: Folders and files of an archive, or of one of its folders, whose name holds a text (any case).
get.description:
`q` (at least 2 characters) is looked for in the names of the whole archive, the catalog
looked through for 1000 ms at most per request: a page may hold fewer than `limit`
(default 100, at most 1000) and still have a `next` (ask again with `after`). Each
item has `where`, the path of its folder. With `folder` (a folder's id), only what is right inside that
folder, in its order (folders first, by name), without `where`. 202 while the list is read, as for
`GET explore`.

get.summary: One file inside an archive, decompressed as it is read: for the viewer, or downloaded.
get.description:
`archive` is the archive's path, UTF-8 in base64url; `id` the entry's id in its listing; `name` its name
(the browser's file name). Sandboxed as the library's files are, inline only for what the browser shows
safely (pictures, audio, video, plain text), downloaded otherwise or with `download=true`. Larger than
`Files:Archives:MaxPreviewMegabytes` only with `download=true` (413 `too-large` otherwise). An
entry claiming more than `Files:Archives:MaxCompressionRatio` times its packed size is refused (422);
one that would unpack more than `Files:Archives:MaxSkippedMegabytes` of the files before it (a solid 7z
or rar, a compressed tar) too (413 `too-large`: extract it). Its data is held to the size the
archive declares: more or less is a broken archive, and the download is cut off. `unlock` (from
`unlock`) opens an encrypted entry, or any of an archive whose list is encrypted.

get.summary: One file inside an archive by its path in the archive, as `entry/{archive}/{id}/{name}` serves it.
get.description:
`at` is the file's path inside the archive (folders separated by `/`; as written, else in any case): the
address the links and pictures of a document of the archive lead to. The same rights, checks and answers
as by id.

get.summary: A text file inside an archive, decoded as `GET api/files/text` decodes a library file; read only.
get.description:
`id` is the entry's id in the archive's listing (or `at` its path in the archive); `encoding` reads it
in that encoding rather than the one it seems to have. Up to 10 MB
(413 `too-large`: download it); 415 `not-text` when it isn't text. `access`
allows nothing: an entry is never saved over. The same checks as `GET explore/entry` (password,
compression ratio, files before it in a solid block).

post.summary: Tries a password on an archive; answers an unlock for the requests that need it.
post.description:
Checked on the archive itself: its encrypted list (7z, rar), else its smallest encrypted file read
through (its checks and authentication). 422 (`wrong-password`) for a wrong one, 409
(`not-protected`) for an archive that has nothing encrypted, 202 while its list is still being
read. At most 10 a minute per caller (429). The password stays in the
server's memory only, behind the unlock: never logged, never answered; the unlock serves its caller
only, for this archive as it is, until 15 minutes unused or a sign-out.

get.summary: Settings of a level, with the values in effect and, for each, where it comes from and whether it can be changed.
get.description:
`level` is `server` (the server settings page, over the configuration files: server administrators) or
`tenant` (the library's settings, over the server's). Without it: `server` for server administrators,
`tenant` otherwise. The library root, the database, ffmpeg and the system commands are only set in the
configuration files.

put.summary: Saves the settings of a level; they apply right away.
put.description:
`level` is `server` (the server settings page, over the configuration files: server administrators) or
`tenant` (the library's settings, over the server's). Without it: `server` for server administrators,
`tenant` otherwise. The library root, the database, ffmpeg and the system commands are only set in the
configuration files.
Only the settings the level may change are kept, when they differ from what it inherits. Changing
one it may not change (locked above, outside its scope, or without the section's right) is a
validation error.

patch.summary: Saves only the settings sent (and lock changes) at a level; the others keep what the level has.
patch.description:
`level` is `server` (the server settings page, over the configuration files: server administrators) or
`tenant` (the library's settings, over the server's). Without it: `server` for server administrators,
`tenant` otherwise. The library root, the database, ffmpeg and the system commands are only set in the
configuration files.
`values` maps setting keys (`player.seekSeconds`) to their new value; one equal to what the level
inherits follows the levels above again. `lock` / `unlock` list the settings this level starts or
stops locking for the levels below. The values are checked with those in effect; nothing is saved
when one is refused.

delete.summary: Forgets a level's values: the levels above apply again.
delete.description:
`level` is `server` (the server settings page, over the configuration files: server administrators) or
`tenant` (the library's settings, over the server's). Without it: `server` for server administrators,
`tenant` otherwise. The library root, the database, ffmpeg and the system commands are only set in the
configuration files.

put.summary: Locks settings at a level: the levels below (libraries, users) cannot change them.
put.description:
`level` is `server` (the server settings page, over the configuration files: server administrators) or
`tenant` (the library's settings, over the server's). Without it: `server` for server administrators,
`tenant` otherwise. The library root, the database, ffmpeg and the system commands are only set in the
configuration files.

get.summary: The signed-in user's own preferences (theme, page sizes, player...) over the library's settings.

put.summary: Saves the signed-in user's own preferences; settings locked by the library or the server cannot change.

patch.summary: Saves only the preferences sent (`values` by setting key); the others stay as they are.

delete.summary: Forgets the signed-in user's preferences: the library's settings apply again.

get.summary: The signed-in user's quick links in the library, in order, with whether each one is still there.

post.summary: Adds folders and files to the quick links, or moves those already there; answers the whole list.
post.description:
Every new path must be a folder or file of the library. A list holds at most 100
links: an addition going past it is refused as a whole.

delete.summary: Removes the quick link to `path` (the folder or file stays); answers the whole list.

get.summary: Where the library browsed is on the server's disk, and the ffmpeg executable found.
Downloads a backup (zip) of the databases and the configuration files.
get.description:
The databases of the accounts and of every library's index (SQLite: copied while the app keeps working;
SQL Server: `BACKUP DATABASE … COPY_ONLY`, see `Sfe:Backup:SqlServerFolder`), `settings.json`, the
`appsettings*.json` of the content root, a `manifest.json` saying where each came from and a
`README.txt`. Thumbnail and trickplay caches are not included. It holds password hashes and connection
strings.

get.summary: Entries of the server's log, newest first: warnings, errors and messages.
get.description:
Filters, all optional: `q` (text found in the message, the logger's name or the exception, ignoring
case), `levels` (comma-separated: `trace`, `debug`, `information`, `warning`, `securityWarning`,
`error`, `critical`; `securityWarning` = security events: wrong passwords, lockouts, wrong setup codes,
recoveries), `from` and `to` (ISO 8601 moments; `to` excluded), `tenant` (a space's id; `0` = the
server's own entries, outside any space). Server administrators see every space's entries; others only
those of their space, whatever `tenant` says. Pages of `limit` entries (default
100, at most 500); pass `next` as `before` for
the following page. The last seconds' entries may not be there yet: the log is written every few
seconds.

get.summary: Whether the space's library folder is kept alive on its file server, and what the last pings found.

post.summary: Pings the space's folders now (also while keep alive is off, as with `Always`), and answers their state.
post.description: Waits for the pings, at most `Sfe:KeepAlive:TimeoutSeconds`; a folder still blocked from an earlier ping is not pinged again.

get.summary: How a kind of connection is set up: offered or not, the return address to register at the provider, and where its app secret comes from (never the secret itself).

put.summary: Sets the secret of the provider's app; kept in a file readable by the server only, never sent back. A secret in the configuration wins over it.

delete.summary: Removes the secret typed for the provider's app (sign-ins go on with PKCE alone).

post.summary: Checks the kind's settings with the provider when it can (app key and secret).
Begins making a connection: checks what is asked, then answers the provider's address to send the browser to (and the state it comes back with), or the connection when no more is needed.
Begins signing a connection in again (its sign-in was refused or lost): the same connection, groups and rules afterwards. Its owner (account level) or who manages its level.
Ends a sign-in with what the person brings back (the code the provider shows). A state is used once, by the account that began it, within 10 minutes.

get.summary: Where the provider sends the browser back: ends the sign-in begun by this session's account and redirects into the web client (`connections?made=`, `?reconnected=` or `?error=`).
The connections this session may use in its library (and how far), and those it manages: its own, its library's, the server's; the server's administrators also see every account's, to remove.

patch.summary: Renames a connection, turns it off or on, makes it read only, or roots it at another folder.

delete.summary: Removes a connection with who uses it; the files at the provider are left as they are.

put.summary: Offers a server-level connection to every library or to some; a library no longer offered loses its groups' access.
The groups of the request's library that use a connection of that library, or a server-level one offered to it: Read or Write, replacing those it had there.

get.summary: Lists a folder of a connection (folders first).
get.description:
The listing of `GET api/browse` (`listing`), with how far the session uses the connection (`access`) and
what its provider can do (`capabilities`). A folder the library's index holds whole (synced recently, the
folder listed) is read from the index: sorted by the database, counted, any size. Otherwise the first page
(`offset` 0) reads the folder from the provider and the next ones reuse that read for a few minutes; items
the index doesn't hold yet have `indexed` false. A folder too large to read whole from the provider comes in
its order (`sorted` false) and `hasMore` tells that the next pages read on. A connection whose sign-in the
provider no longer accepts answers 409 `connection-needs-reconnecting`; the provider asking to wait, 429
`connection-rate-limited` with `Retry-After`; the provider unreachable, 502 `connection-unavailable`.

get.summary: Streams a file of a connection (one HTTP range when the provider reads parts).
get.description: `download=true` asks the browser to save it, which needs the right `files.download`.

get.summary: JPEG preview of a picture or video of a connection, made by its provider.
The properties of a file or folder of a connection (`path` empty: its root folder).
get.description:
The item as a listing shows it (`item`; the root folder named after the connection), the provider's kind,
the content hash the provider gives (`contentHash`, of the kind `hashName` names) and whether the file has
content to download. `account` (the provider's account) is given only on the caller's own connection.

post.summary: Creates a folder in a connection.
post.description:
400 with `errors.name` for a name no provider takes (or this one refuses), 404 when the folder is not
there, 409 `file-exists` when something of that name is. A renamed folder's rules follow it
for every library; 409 `folder-rules` when the library's rules are set where it goes.

post.summary: Renames a file or folder of a connection, in its folder.
post.description:
400 with `errors.name` for a name no provider takes (or this one refuses), 404 when the folder is not
there, 409 `file-exists` when something of that name is. A renamed folder's rules follow it
for every library; 409 `folder-rules` when the library's rules are set where it goes.

post.summary: Deletes files and folders of a connection.
post.description:
Deletes each of `paths` (at most 1000) into the provider's own trash when it has one; `permanent` is
ignored. Each item's `status` says what became of it (`trashId` is always null).

post.summary: Moves or copies files and folders of a connection into one of its folders.
post.description:
`kind` `move` or `copy`, each of `paths` (at most 1000) into the folder `target`, done by the provider.
`conflict`: `fail` (status `exists`), `keepBoth` (the provider's numbering) or `replace` (a file only; a
folder is never replaced). An item moved where it is is `skipped`; a folder into itself `invalid`. 409
`connection-not-supported` when the provider cannot move or copy on its side. A moved folder's
rules follow it for every library (`conflict` status when the library's are set where it goes); a move
letting more of the library's people see or change a folder answers 409 `access-gains`
with its `gains` (as `api/files/jobs/check`) unless `keepAccess` is given (true pins their current access).

get.summary: Where the index of a connection's files stands in the request's library: files and folders, last sync, a full listing under way, what stopped the last sync, what the running one does.
get.description: For who manages the connection (404 otherwise, and for a server's connection not offered to the library). Nothing is indexed before the connection is first opened in the library.

post.summary: Syncs the index of a connection's files in the request's library now (in the background).
post.description: 202 with the status (`running` already true when a sync was running: none is added). 409 `connection-unusable` for a connection that is off. Each sync is a run of the "Connection index" task (history and log).

post.summary: Which of these names are already taken in a connection's folder.
Starts an upload into a connection.
post.description:
Checks the folder and the name (a path below the folder for a folder upload, each part a name any provider
takes) and opens an upload session at the provider; answers the upload (201) with its `id`. At most
20 unfinished uploads per person (429), dropped after
24 hours without a chunk. 409 `connection-not-supported`
when the provider cannot take a file in parts.

get.summary: The caller's unfinished uploads into a connection.
One of the caller's unfinished uploads into a connection: how much the provider has.

put.summary: Passes a chunk (the body) on to the provider at `offset`.
put.description:
The body goes on to the provider at once. `offset` must be the bytes the provider has: another one answers
409 with the upload, to resend from there. A chunk passing the size, 16
MB or the provider's part limit is refused (400).

delete.summary: Cancels one of the caller's unfinished uploads into a connection.

post.summary: Makes the file of a fully sent upload in its folder of the connection.
post.description:
`conflicts`: `ask` (409 `file-exists` when the name is taken), `replace` (a file only, by
the provider; needs `files.delete`), `skip` (the upload is dropped, 204), `keepBoth` (the provider's
numbering). Folders on the way are made by the provider. Answers the new file as listings show it.

post.summary: Names the files and folders of a connection's zip; answers the link that downloads it.
post.description:
At most 10,000 items, checked at the provider; a folder brings everything in it. The link
works once, for the caller, within 2 minutes; 429 when the caller
already downloads 2 zips.

get.summary: Downloads a zip named by CreateConnectionArchive (once); what has no content is listed in “SFE - left out.txt”.
The request's library's folder rules in a connection.

put.summary: Replaces the request's library's folder rules in a connection; answers them.
put.description:
The body lists every rule of the request's library in the connection: those left out are removed. A group
uses the connection only with its level given in `PUT …/groups`; a rule may then hide a folder or change its
level there. At most 250 rules; none on an account's connection. A rule without
`itemId` gets its folder's id from the provider when it can (at most 50 looked
up per change): it then also applies where the folder is renamed or moved outside the app.

get.summary: The sub-folders of a folder of a connection, for choosing where a rule goes (every folder, whatever rules apply to the asker).

accessToken.description:
A personal access token (My account › Access tokens), sent as `Authorization: Bearer sfe_…`. Without one,
the browser's session cookie is used. Routes marked `x-sfe-session-only` refuse tokens (403
`session-only`).
